title: Operating Card Provenance Recovery
summary: For intermediate practitioners, this decision path explains whether the operating card can be corrected safely. It identifies the evidence required before operational guidance can be restored or changed.
prerequisites: First-party documentation for the subject of the operating card
Access to the catalogue identifier registry

sections.title: Can this operating card be corrected safely?
paragraphs: No. The supported answer for an intermediate practitioner is to stop before changing or following the operating procedure. The existing resource, its operational claims, and authoritative first-party documentation were not supplied, so the procedure and its expected result are UNKNOWN and are omitted.

The cited item under review is content/resources/coding-tools/continue-operating-card.json. It is a repository path with an unregistered publisher and no previous verification date, not a directly accessible HTTPS source. Whether an earlier source moved or merely exceeded its review cadence is UNKNOWN. No affected statement can therefore be identified or corrected truthfully.

sections.title: Recovery decision path
paragraphs: First, recover the complete existing JSON object and preserve a verbatim copy as the comparison baseline. If the object cannot be recovered, stop the update and obtain it from repository history rather than reconstructing its wording or metadata.

Second, identify the previous source title, publisher, HTTPS URL, verification date, and relevant revision or redirect record. If that evidence does not establish whether the source moved or exceeded its cadence, record the change status as UNKNOWN and do not attribute a correction to the source.

Third, obtain current first-party documentation that supports each retained or corrected operational action, expected state, failure mode, and remediation. If a procedure step lacks first-party support or a failed step has no supported next action, omit that step until the missing documentation is available.

Fourth, check every source URL directly over HTTPS and review its contents before assigning a verification date. If a URL does not open directly, replace it with a current first-party URL and repeat the content review. If no qualifying source exists, do not publish operational claims.

Fifth, compare the proposed object with the recovered baseline and retain every field and passage not affected by the documented source change. If the comparison contains unrelated edits, revert those edits and repeat the comparison.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is the recovered baseline, a first-party change record or current first-party documentation, directly accessible HTTPS sources, and a comparison showing only the citation correction and statements demonstrably affected by that correction. If any item is missing, keep the update blocked and request that specific item.

Verify that the final file contains one JSON object and no surrounding text. RFC 8259 defines a JSON object as a permitted serialized JSON value, and JSON.parse reports invalid JSON with a SyntaxError. If parsing fails, remove non-JSON text or correct the invalid syntax, then parse the complete file again.

Verify that every source entry has a direct HTTPS URL and a non-future full date in YYYY-MM-DD form. If either check fails, correct the URL or date and repeat the check. Verify catalogue-wide identifier uniqueness against the complete identifier registry; if the registry is unavailable or a duplicate is found, stop publication until the registry is obtained or the identifier conflict is resolved.

This evidence is not currently complete. The source-change cause, affected operational statements, preservation-only comparison, URL-resolution results, and catalogue-wide identifier uniqueness remain UNKNOWN.
